messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're finalizing routing + DNS failover behaviour for the new ap-southeast region. Need clear ownership and a short runbook before we open routing to prod. Questions: who owns DNS failover policy, TTL, and the healthcheck config?
kevin: I can take DNS policy and TTL guidance. Proposal: 30s TTL for failover records (short to meet our RTO), healthcheck at ALB level with two consecutive failures to mark unhealthy. Anyone opposed? :thinking_face:
lucy: 30s TTL SGTM for customer-facing endpoints. For internal service-to-service endpoints I'd prefer 60s to avoid flapping on transient blips. We should list which hostnames are customer-facing vs internal.
maria: Good call. I'll attach the hostname list to the infra ticket. Kevin, can you add the actual DNS change PR and a short config snippet so SREs can review?
kevin: Yup, opened a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/412 — includes route policy + healthcheck configs. Please review. Quick snippet from the PR:

```yaml
- hostname: inference.ap-southeast.redwood.ai
  type: failover
  ttl: 30
  healthcheck:
    path: /_hc
    interval: 10
    unhealthy_threshold: 2
```

kevin: Also added a fallback CNAME to the eu primary pool for the first rollout phase. We'll switch to regional primary after capacity cutover.
maria: @lucy can you own the runbook that covers: DNS rollback steps, healthcheck tuning, who to page for cross-region capacity issues, and verification commands? Keep it short (1-2 pages). Deadline EOW.
lucy: On it. Will add a short checklist and the verification commands. Draft link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/region-apac-runbook (will set perms).
lucy: For verification commands, thinking of these quick checks:
- `dig +short inference.ap-southeast.redwood.ai` -> should return CNAME to failover target or regional A records
- `curl -v https://inference.ap-southeast.redwood.ai/_hc` -> 200 OK
- `aws elb describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn>` -> confirm healthy count

anton: Heads-up on data residency dependency: private deployments for some customers require logs to stay in-region. We need to confirm whether any failover behaviour would redirect logs out-of-region during failover. Is that tracked?
kevin: Good catch. By default failover CNAME points to eu for now — that would route traffic (and potentially some logs) to eu. We need to add a flag on the routing policy for "no-cross-region-data" to block failover for residency-constrained customers. I'll add a config toggle to the PR.
maria: Action items: kevin add toggle + update PR, lucy publish runbook and share link, anton compile list of residency customers (if any) and we will do a manual opt-in for failover. I'll own the final sign-off.
sre-bot: deploybot: routing/pr-412 passed CI checks and scheduled for staging deploy at 2026-03-18T02:30Z :white_check_mark:
kevin: pinging eng-sre reviewers @anton @lucy — please review routing PR and the toggle change. If no blockers I'll plan staging cutover tomorrow night.
lucy: Reviewing now, will leave comments. If all good, tagging oncall for staged test next window. :eyes:
anton: Reviewing too, will confirm residency list by EOD. If anyone needs me to run the staged failover test, ping my handle.
maria: Thanks all. I'll summarize in the infra ticket and move to "ready for staging" once PR + runbook are linked.
